The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

That accident happened [A] /a long time ago, but [B] / I have shivered at [C] / the thought of it ever for [D].
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 
The error lies in part D – “the thought of it ever for” is grammatically incorrect.

 
 
• 
 
The expression “ever for” is not used in English. The word “ever” is generally used with “since” or “after” to express continuity of time from a particular event in the past up to the present.

 
 
• 
 
The correct phrase should therefore be “ever since”, meaning from that time until now.

 
 
• 
 
The sentence talks about a lasting emotional reaction — the speaker has continued to shiver whenever they think of the accident. To show this continued effect, the present perfect tense (“I have shivered”) must be followed by a phrase indicating continuity, i.e., “ever since.”

 
 
• 
 
Hence, the correct sentence will be:

 “That accident happened a long time ago, but I have shivered at the thought of it ever since.”

 
 
• 
 
This corrected version expresses that even though the accident occurred long ago, its emotional impact still remains with the speaker.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *“That accident happened a long time ago, but I have shivered at the thought of it ever since.”*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A:** “That accident happened” – grammatically correct, simple past tense used properly.
 
• **B:** “a long time ago, but” – correct use of a time expression and conjunction.
 
• **C:** “I have shivered at” – correct present perfect tense to indicate an ongoing feeling.
 
• **D:** “the thought of it ever for” – incorrect phrase; should be “ever since.”

In the following question, a sentence is given in Passive Voice. Out of the four options, select the one which best expresses the sentence in Active Voice. 

A house has been built by Mr. White.

options.text: Mr. White has built a house.
Mr. White have built a house.
Mr. White have build a house.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is, **Mr. White has built a house.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **Present Perfect tense.**
 
• There are certain rules for changing the voice of such sentences
 
• Active Voice**:** Subject+have/has + verb+object 
 
• Passive Voice**:** Object+ have/has+ been+ third form of verb+by+suject
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is, *Mr. White has built a house**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Let us see where present perfect tense is used:

 
• to indicate activities that have been completed in the recent past.

 **Example:** *I have just finished my cooking*

 
• to show an action that began in the past and is continuing up to the present moment

 **Example:** *We have known each other for the past ten years*

 
• to show the past actions whose time is not given

 **Example:** *I have lived in Delhi*

The correct sentence is, *Mr. White has built a house.*

questions.solution:

• The amendment of Constitution can be initiated by the** introduction of a bill in either house of the Parliament**. (does not in the legislature)

• It must be passed in each house by a **special majority**. (the majority of the total membership of the house and a majority of 2/3rd of the members of house present and voting)
 
• Each house must **pass the bill separately**. (no provision for joint sittings)
 
• If the bill is for amending the **federal structure of the Constitution**, then it must be ratified by the legislature of half of the states by a simple majority. (the majority of the members of house present and voting)

questions.question: Which of the following may cause the breakdown of pyruvate into lactic acid in our muscles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lack of Oxygen.**__

__**Explanation:**__

 
• When the body has plenty of oxygen, pyruvate is shuttled to an aerobic pathway to be further broken down for more energy.
 
• But when oxygen is limited, the body temporarily converts pyruvate into a substance called lactate, which allows glucose breakdown and thus energy production continues.
 
• The first step of respiration is the breakdown of glucose, a six-carbon molecule, into a three-carbon molecule called pyruvate.
 
• This process takes place in the cytoplasm.
 
• Further, the pyruvate may be converted into ethanol and carbon dioxide. This process takes place in yeast during fermentation. Since this process takes place in the absence of air (oxygen), it is called anaerobic respiration.
 
• Breakdown of pyruvate using oxygen takes place in the mitochondria. This process breaks up the three-carbon pyruvate molecule to give three molecules of carbon dioxide. The other product is water. Since this process takes place in the presence of air (oxygen), it is called aerobic respiration.
 
• The release of energy in this aerobic process is a lot greater than in the anaerobic process.
 
• Sometimes, when there is a lack of oxygen in the muscle cells, another pathway for the breakdown of pyruvate is taken.
 
• Here the pyruvate is converted into lactic acid which is also a three-carbon molecule.
 
• This build-up of lactic acid in our muscles during sudden activities like exercise causes cramps.
